summary.headline: Xtranet Q2 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to about Rs 110 crore, with PAT up 111% to about Rs 14 crore and EBITDA margin at 20.42%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of about Rs 110 crore (+63% YoY) and H1 revenue of about Rs 160 crore (+42%), with H1 operational EBITDA of about Rs 33 crore at 20.49% margin. Government and PSU share of business has fallen to about 30-35% from roughly 75-80% earlier, per the CFO. A new data center subsidiary was formed, with an initial 2 MW build at an estimated Rs 130-140 crore. Management said working capital rose during H1 and operating cash flow was negative, and it reiterated FY27 revenue ambition above original guidance of Rs 500 crore. Several analyst questions on cash flow, receivables and IPO capex were answered only partially on the call.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 24.38 crore (per analyst, not disputed by management)

segments.name: Data center infrastructure and IT operations
segments.commentary: Largest vertical and key growth driver; management says over 50% of the pipeline sits here. Company has over 1 MW hosted capacity and about 2 MW internal demand, currently served from third-party data centers.

segments.name: Enterprise applications (ERP)
segments.commentary: Lower-margin vertical, per CFO at about 25-26% margin versus 34-35% earlier. XERP is being pitched to small and mid-market firms; management cited XtraBanks deployed in 60+ banks.

segments.name: Digital transformation services
segments.commentary: Higher-margin, growing vertical; management cites AI-led projects and services growth as reducing dependence on supply chain. No separate revenue figure given.

segments.name: Proprietary platforms (XtraTrust and Synergy)
segments.commentary: Together contribute 14% of revenue per management. XtraTrust is a MeitY-approved certifying authority; about 1 million B2C subscribers and 80+ B2B clients; 100+ government portals accept its digital signatures. Individual revenue, EBITDA and recurring split not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management ambition is to surpass original FY27 revenue guidance while sustaining strong EBITDA and PAT margins; an analyst cited Rs 500 crore FY27 guidance from the prior call, and management said it is hopeful of achieving it with Q3 and Q4 heavily loaded.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at about 17.5-18% going forward, per CFO.
Working capital cycle expected to improve by about 15-20 days by year-end FY27 versus FY26.
International revenue expected to start from Q4 FY27; six-country proposals in Middle East and Africa under negotiation, with 10-15 year contract tenors.
Data center: initial 2 MW build at Rs 130-140 crore funded by internal accruals and debt; scale-up to 10 MW under an asset-light model still being worked out, with figures to follow.
capex_capacity: Data center subsidiary formed in Q2 for hosting, cloud and managed services; initial 2 MW build at about Rs 130-140 crore, with expansion to about 10 MW planned.

Rs 8.48 crore IPO capex allocation not yet utilised; management said it is for equipment for the IT park, with the first 42,000 sq ft block aligned and deployment expected to be allocated in the current quarter.
Procurement and supply chain strengthened in H1 to secure hardware and software; management says OEM supply has improved, though Q1 was weak.
demand_pricing: Fresh orders of about Rs 90 crore in Q2 FY27; order book about Rs 390 crore at 30 Sep 2026, with 50-55% expected to bill in FY27.
Bid pipeline above Rs 2,000 crore; 25-30% of pipeline typically converts into firm orders.
Order book walk per management: about Rs 350 crore at start of year, about Rs 200 crore of new orders in the year (25% existing customers, 75% new logos), about Rs 160 crore executed.
Government and PSU share down to about 30-35% of business from about 47% of FY26 revenue as cited in the opening remarks; CFO said 50-50 government/enterprise at FY26 close.
Competitive positioning: XERP targeted at small and mid-market (about 100,000 MSMEs) where Oracle and SAP are seen as too costly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the proposed investment, timeline and funding for the new data center subsidiary, and what capacity and revenue are envisaged?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial 2 MW build needs about Rs 130-140 crore, funded partly by internal accruals and partly by debt; expansion to 10 MW is on a different, asset-light financial model still being worked out. Specific numbers to follow.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate its data center and cloud offering from established operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited over 1 MW hosted capacity and about 2 MW internal demand from its own SaaS applications, to be hosted on its own platform and later offered as public cloud.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin expansion and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix shift: lower-margin enterprise business (about 25-26% margin, down from 34-35%) is shrinking while digital services, proprietary platforms and data center grow. Sustainable margin guided at about 17.5-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the government share fell from about 75-80% to 30-35%, and the working capital cycle is expected to improve by 15-20 days by year-end versus FY26. The analyst's day-count figures were partly garbled on the line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book split between fresh and repeat business, and which verticals drive inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about Rs 200 crore new orders, 25% from existing customers and 75% from new logos; data center and IT operations and digital/AI projects plus proprietary platforms are the focus areas.

qa_highlights.question: How consistent has order-to-revenue conversion been, and what are typical execution timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was low due to supply chain issues; management says supply has since streamlined. Infrastructure deployments take 90 days to 18 months followed by 5-10 years of O&M; enterprise application deployments take 4-6 months plus 5-6 years of support; B2B PKI deployments take 30-90 days; B2C is subscription-based (1-3 years).

qa_highlights.question: What progress has been made internationally, and are there signed contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Proposals submitted in six countries across the Middle East and Africa, under negotiation; none signed yet. Contracts are expected to run 10-15 years, with revenue starting around Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive standing in the DSC market and XERP versus Oracle?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust cited 24x7 online issuance within 15-30 minutes, integrations with PAN, Aadhaar, GST and banks, and availability on web, Android and iOS. XERP is positioned for small and mid-market firms, with banking solutions deployed in 60+ banks.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow negative despite strong PAT, what is the collection timeline for the Rs 24.38 crore receivables increase, and what are the revenue, EBITDA and recurring split for XtraTrust and Synergy?
qa_highlights.answer: Not answered directly. Management said the receivables rise reflects invoices raised in late September for recently delivered projects, expected to be collected in October and within Q2 FY27. Management said the XtraTrust and Synergy breakdown was in the uploaded presentation and offered to answer in writing; the cash flow reason was not explained. The IPO capex question was answered (see capex section).

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you of the Rs 500 crore FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 execution will be heavily loaded in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years, and it is hopeful of hitting the target.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in H1 despite PAT of about Rs 20 crore; receivables up Rs 24.38 crore and working capital build for procurement. Watch Q3 OCF and receivable days.
Revenue back-loaded into Q3 and Q4 to reach guidance; H1 revenue of about Rs 160 crore would need a steep H2 ramp versus a Rs 500 crore FY27 target.
Order book of Rs 390 crore is well below the target path; conversion of Rs 2,000 crore+ pipeline (25-30% historical conversion) is the key swing factor.
Supply chain dependence for OEM hardware in data center projects; Q1 execution was weak.
Data center plan is asset-heavy (Rs 130-140 crore for 2 MW) despite the stated asset-light model for scale-up; funding mix and returns not specified.
Disclosure gaps: no split for XtraTrust and Synergy revenue, EBITDA or recurring revenue; no order-book-to-revenue numbers beyond H1; several analyst questions were deferred to written responses.
Q2 Rs 24.38 crore receivable collections in October not yet verified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and pipeline, but evasive on cash flow and receivables: the operating cash flow question was not answered and several numeric questions were deferred to the presentation or to written replies.
key_quotes: We delivered a successful quarter with exceptional growth and robust execution momentum across all our business verticals.
While this has temporarily increased our working capital requirements, we believe these investments will support stronger execution, revenue growth, and profitability during H2 FY'27.
The momentum achieved during H1 gives us confidence in our full-year performance, and our ambition is to surpass our original revenue guidance while sustaining strong EBITDA and PAT margins.

adds.what: Initial 2 MW data center build (new data center subsidiary)

growth.why: Management's ambition is to surpass the original Rs 500 crore FY27 revenue guidance, hopeful with Q3 and Q4 heavily loaded, backed by a Rs 390 crore order book (Rs 50-55% billing in FY27 per brief) and a Rs 2,000 crore+ bid pipeline, though the 2 MW data center build (Rs 130-140 crore) is approved with no live date and the 10 MW scale-up figures are still to follow.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin sustained at about 17.5-18% versus H1 operational EBITDA margin of 20.49%, so the guide sits below current levels; mix shift away from 25-26% margin enterprise business is the driver, but the guide implies some give-back from H1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Initial 2 MW data center build at Rs 130-140 crore is approved with no live date, and the IPO-funded IT park equipment (Rs 8.48 crore, first 42,000 sq ft block) is expected to be allocated in the current quarter; 10 MW scale-up figures are still to follow.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 fresh orders about Rs 90 crore, order book about Rs 390 crore with 50-55% expected to bill in FY27, and H1 revenue up 42% YoY to about Rs 160 crore, though H2 must ramp steeply to reach Rs 500 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The 10 MW scale-up is planned but its funding and figures are still being worked out, and the 2 MW build is already committed at Rs 130-140 crore, so further data center capex disclosure is likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is only hopeful of hitting the Rs 500 crore FY27 target with Q3 and Q4 heavily loaded, and the Rs 390 crore order book is well short of the target path, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 500 crore FY27 target requires a steep H2 ramp from H1 revenue of about Rs 160 crore, Q1 was weak on supply chain, and H1 operating cash flow was negative with receivables up Rs 24.38 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: International revenue is expected to start in Q4 FY27 from six-country Middle East and Africa proposals under negotiation with none signed, and XERP is being pitched to about 100,000 MSMEs, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: International revenue from Middle East and Africa
rows.why: Proposals submitted in six countries, none signed yet, with 10-15 year contract tenors and revenue expected to start around Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Working capital cycle improvement of 15-20 days
rows.why: CFO guided a 15-20 day improvement versus FY26 by year-end, but H1 operating cash flow was negative and receivables rose Rs 24.38 crore, so the path is unproven.

rows.label: Bid pipeline conversion
rows.why: Bid pipeline is above Rs 2,000 crore and 25-30% typically converts, implying roughly Rs 500-600 crore of potential orders, but conversion depends on bids being won.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, margin sustainability and the Rs 2,000 crore+ pipeline, but cautious and evasive on operating cash flow, receivables and the XtraTrust/Synergy split; analysts pushed on cash flow, working capital days and how the Rs 500 crore FY27 target can be reached.
